gaps.title: Squad-to-battalion small-UAS fleet control, registry, deconfliction, tasking and collection forwarding for Drone Dominance mass (multi-vendor drones into company/battalion C2, S2 and training pipelines)
gaps.problem: Hundreds of thousands of multi-vendor small drones are being pushed to squads faster than units can register, deconflict, task and report them into company/battalion C2, and the EO/IR video they collect mostly dies at the controller because the Army's fusion node (TITAN) fields only 17 units at division/corps.
gaps.user: Company/battalion drone team leaders and sUAS operators, S2/S3/S6 sections, brigade collection managers, C-UAS operators, Transformation-in-Contact units, TITAN operators as upstream consumers

gaps.title: Vendor-agnostic automated PACE/multi-path transport orchestration and single-pane tactical NetOps for S6/G6 at brigade and below (MANET, pLEO, GEO, private 5G, HF)
gaps.problem: Units carry three to five transports but path selection and failover are still planned on paper and executed by signal soldiers using many vendor tools that do not share data, so applications stall during jamming or movement and awareness of link health, spectrum conflicts and cyber events is manual and slow.
gaps.user: Brigade S6 and division G6 NetOps cells, platform crews at brigade and below, NGC2 transport-layer integrators, NETCOM

gaps.title: Sensor-agnostic own-signature/EM COP fusion as a TAK plugin, with disconnected tactical spectrum management (JRFL, assignments, interference tickets) and emitter-library distribution to cheap sensor fleets
gaps.problem: Units are receiving thousands of heterogeneous cheap spectrum sensors (MOTH, Dragonfly, manpacks, S2AS kits) but there is no government-owned, sensor-agnostic layer that fuses them into a real-time own-signature and threat-emitter picture inside TAK/EWPMT-X under DDIL, and brigade spectrum managers still build frequency plans and interference reports with tools that need reach-back to DISA's legacy Spectrum XXI.
gaps.user: Brigade and division CEMA sections, EW platoon leaders, Army 25E and USMC spectrum managers, JFMO and JEMSO cell staff, EW reprogramming centers (Army, 350th SWW), brigade EW technicians

gaps.title: Brigade-and-below multinational SA/C2 bridge and releasability-aware coalition COP federation (productized Mission Partner Kit with partner-specific views and federated partner identity across TAK, SitaWare and national systems)
gaps.problem: U.S. and allied tactical units cannot quickly share position, geometry, chat and voice across national C2 systems, so regiments build ad hoc kits, coalition users are managed as guests on separate enclaves, and release decisions rest on liaison officers, translation gateways and manual sanitization rather than tagged objects and federated identities.
gaps.user: Battalion/brigade S3/S6 and fires cells, coalition liaison officers, allied battalion staffs and partner-nation battle captains, MPE administrators, foreign disclosure officers, combatant command MPE managers, NATO FMN node operators
